His son Peter subsequently took over direction of the business, which became Aegeus Shipping.

long_biography.plain_text:
Greek shipowner Markos Petros Nomikos helped finance Thermo Electron when his son Peter and engineer George Hatsopoulos sought to commercialise a device that converted heat into electricity. In 1955, he supplied their initial $50,000 after an approach through his bridge partner, Hatsopoulos's uncle Costas Platsis.

Nomikos initially expected the venture to fail and his son to return to the family shipping business. Instead, as the company grew, he continued providing capital beyond his original contribution. Trained in law, he also contributed regularly to the maritime journal Naftika Chronika, writing about the industry's problems and future.
